description: No glazing at all, which on a street of shopfronts is the thing you notice before you notice the smell. The building is a counter with a roof on it: a marble slab the full width of the frontage, canted toward you, open to the street behind a canvas awning let down on two poles, and a crushed-ice bed on the slab with the morning on it in rows. The ice melts off the front edge all day and runs into the gutter, and there is a strip of pavement outside this shop that has not been dry since anybody can remember. The name is painted on the fascia in blue on white, and the lettering is a great deal older than the man behind the slab.
name: The Codfather
